name: code-aster
raw_meta_yaml:
schema_version: 1

context:
  name: code-aster
  version: "18.1.7"
  sha256: cdaaa8743dba56f298e2279518ee718cb73eb4f6b9048713b8a6413f6defb88a
  # Enter build number here
  build: 2
  # this is where the final build number is calculated depending on the matrix of python/mpi variants
  mpi_num: ${{ 100 if mpi == 'nompi' else 0 }}
  build_num: ${{ build + mpi_num }}
  mpi_prefix: ${{ mpi or 'nompi' }}
  # code-aster-tests (noarch) is built, and the full testcase set used, only in the nompi job of the lowest python
  tests_python: ${{ python_min }}
  is_tests_job: ${{ mpi == 'nompi' and (python | version_to_buildstring) == (tests_python | replace('.', '')) }}

recipe:
  name: ${{ name|lower }}
  version: ${{ version }}

source:
  - url: https://gitlab.com/codeaster/src/-/archive/${{ version }}/src-${{ version }}.tar.gz
    sha256: ${{ sha256 }}
    patches:
      - patches/make_shared_use_env_FC_fallback.patch
      # numpy >= 2.4: trapz was removed, int() of a 1-element array raises;
      # medcoupling python 3.13 bindings: MEDFileFields iterator is not iterable
      - patches/numpy_py313_compat.patch
      # petsc >= 3.25 Fortran modules export interfaces that clash with aster_petsc_module.F90
      - patches/petsc_3_25_compat.patch
      # Windows: MSVC (clang-cl) + Intel ifx toolchain, .def exports and pybind11 proxy modules
      - if: win
        then: patches/windows_msvc_ifx.patch
  # code_aster prerequisites sources (only homard is built from it); 18.0.2+ requires version 20251026
  # https://gitlab.com/codeaster-opensource-documentation/opensource-installation-development/-/blob/main/devel/changelog.md
  - if: unix
    then:
      url: https://gitlab.com/api/v4/projects/codeaster-opensource-documentation%2Fopensource-installation-development/packages/generic/codeaster-prerequisites/20251026/codeaster-prerequisites-20251026-oss.tar.gz
      sha256: e450bbbee0047cf17f6f9423400a7ac83fc633e6e62e596111825016e945e7df
      target_directory: codeaster-prerequisites/

build:
  number: ${{ build_num }}
  # Windows: sequential only (no MPI MUMPS/PETSc build for ifx)
  skip: osx or (win and mpi != 'nompi') or (python_impl == 'pypy')

outputs:
  - package:
      name: ${{ name }}-tests
      version: ${{ version }}
    build:
      number: ${{ build_num }}
      string: h${{ hash }}_${{ build_num }}
      script: copy_tests.sh
      noarch: generic
      # noarch output: build it in a single CI job only.
      # No variant.ignore_keys here: conda-smithy distributes CI jobs over the intersection of
      # every output's loop vars, so ignoring mpi/python would collapse the matrix into one job.
      skip: not (is_tests_job and linux and x86_64)
    tests:
      - package_contents:
          files:
            - share/aster/tests/forma01a.export
            - share/aster/tests/zzzz121a.export

  - package:
      name: ${{ name }}
      version: ${{ version }}
    build:
      script:
        # build.sh on unix, build.bat on Windows
        file: build
        env:
          ASTER_BUILD_TESTS: ${{ env.get("ASTER_BUILD_TESTS", default="submit") }}
      string: py${{ python | version_to_buildstring }}_${{ mpi_prefix }}_h${{ hash }}_${{ build_num }}
      prefix_detection:
        ignore_binary_files: true
      dynamic_linking:
        rpaths:
          - lib/
          - lib/aster/
          - if: mpi != "nompi"
            then: lib/petsc4py/lib
        missing_dso_allowlist:
          - if: linux
            then:
              - "*/libbibfor.so"
              - "*/libbibfor_ext.so"
              - "*/libbibc.so"
              - "*/libbibcxx.so"
              - "*/libAsterGC.so"
              - lib64/aster/libaster.so

    requirements:
      build:
        - ${{ compiler('c') }}
        - ${{ stdlib('c') }}
        - ${{ compiler('cxx') }}
        - ${{ compiler('fortran') }}
        - if: linux
          then: libgomp
        - cmake <4
        - setuptools
        - if: unix
          then:
            - bison
            - flex
            - swig 4.2.1.*
            # 'mfront --obuild' (CREA_LIB_MFRONT) runs make in the testcases
            - make
        # Windows: C/C++ are compiled with clang-cl against the MSVC toolchain
        - if: win
          then:
            - clang
            # 'waf' is launched by Scripts\waf.exe, bound to the build-env
            # interpreter, so 'data/wscript' imports yaml from there, while the
            # configure check ("Checking for python module 'yaml'") probes the
            # host interpreter. Without this, CFG_EXT is 'yaml' but the build
            # stage raises "NameError: name 'yaml' is not defined".
            - pyyaml
        - waf ==2.1.5
        - if: "mpi != 'nompi'"
          then: ${{ mpi }}
      host:
        - python
        - numpy
        - libboost-devel
        - if: unix
          then:
            - libblas >=3.9.0
            - liblapack >=3.9.0
            - openblas >=0.3.20
        # Windows: MKL, matching the conda-forge ifx MUMPS build
        - if: win
          then:
            - mkl-devel
            - libblas >=3.9.0 *mkl
            - liblapack >=3.9.0 *mkl
            # ifx runtime in PREFIX for the testcases run by build.bat, as in an
            # installed env (run dep below): Python >= 3.8 does not use PATH to
            # resolve extension-module DLL dependencies, so a bare
            # 'import libAsterGC' (ssll13d.py, ssls134b.py) otherwise fails
            - intel-fortran-rt
        - libxml2-devel
        - zlib
        - scotch
        - mfront
        - mgis
        # miss3d (CALC_MISS) on win-64 is an old flang-5/m2w64 build, incompatible with the ifx stack
        - if: unix
          then: miss3d
        - metis
        - hdf5 >=1.14 *${{ mpi }}*
        - libmed * *${{ mpi }}*
        # ParaMEDMEM.CFEMDEC (code_aster.Coupling) requires medcoupling >= 9.16
        - medcoupling >=9.16 *${{ mpi }}*
        - scipy
        - if: unix
          then: mumps-include
        # code_aster calls MUMPS through its Fortran interface: pick the ifx ABI build,
        # which run-exports the matching mumps-seq ifx_*
        - if: win
          then: mumps-seq-fortran-devel * ifx_*
        - if: (mpi == 'nompi') and not win
          then:
            - mumps-seq
        - if: (mpi != 'nompi') and not win
          then:
            - ${{ mpi }}
            - scalapack >=2.2.0,<3
            - mumps-mpi
            - parmetis
            - petsc
            - slepc
            - mpi4py
            - petsc4py
            - slepc4py
      run:
        - ${{ pin_compatible('mgis', upper_bound='x.x') }}
        - ${{ pin_compatible('mfront', upper_bound='x.x.x') }}
        - if: unix
          then: ${{ pin_compatible('miss3d', upper_bound='x.x') }}
        - ${{ pin_compatible('medcoupling', upper_bound='x.x') }}
        - ${{ pin_compatible('libmed', upper_bound='x.x') }}
        - ${{ pin_compatible('numpy', upper_bound='x.x') }}
        - if: unix
          then: libopenblas
        - libxml2-devel
        - python
        - if: linux
          then: libxcrypt
        - scipy
        - if: (mpi != 'nompi') and not win
          then:
            - petsc4py
        # Windows: bibfor.dll/bibfor_ext.dll/AsterGC.dll/dmumps.dll all need
        # the ifx runtime (libifcoremd.dll, libmmd.dll, svml_dispmd.dll).
        # Reproduced directly in a built test env: `import code_aster` raised
        # "Could not load bibc.dll. Error: The specified module could not be
        # found" (bibc.dll itself was found and loaded via its absolute path
        # -- ERROR_MOD_NOT_FOUND there only means one of ITS dependencies
        # didn't resolve); copying these 3 DLLs in was enough to fix it.
        # hdf5/libmed/metis/scotch/mumps-seq are NOT missing -- they're
        # already present transitively via medcoupling/mumps-seq-fortran-
        # devel/mkl's own real dependencies. No run_export carries the ifx
        # runtime itself here: `ifx_win-64` (what compiler('fortran')
        # resolves to) has no run_exports of its own; the strong run_export
        # lives one level down on its dependency ifx_impl_win-64, and that
        # doesn't appear to propagate transitively in this setup.
        - if: win
          then:
            - intel-fortran-rt
            # bibfor.dll links the OpenMP runtime (libomp.dll) directly
            - llvm-openmp
      run_exports:
        - ${{ pin_subpackage('code-aster', upper_bound='x.x') }}

    tests:
      - python:
          imports:
            - code_aster
            - medcoupling
      - package_contents:
          include:
            - asterc_config.h
            - asterf_config.h
          files:
            exists:
              - if: unix
                then:
                  - share/aster/CTestTestfile.cmake
                  - share/aster/run_aster_for_ctest
                else:
                  - Library/share/aster/CTestTestfile.cmake
                  - Library/share/aster/run_aster_for_ctest.bat
            # testcases are shipped by code-aster-tests
            not_exists:
              - share/aster/tests/**
              - Library/share/aster/tests/**
      # This would run ALL sequential (currently passing 99%). Few failures due to missing xmgrace
      #- run_ctest --resutest=${{ env.get("OUTPUT_DIR", default="temp/seq") }}/${{ mpi }} -L submit ${{ '-L sequential' if mpi == 'nompi' else '' }} -LE need_data --timefactor=10.0 --only-failed-results --clean
      - if: is_tests_job and unix
        then:
          # code-aster-tests is built in this job: run against the installed testcases (share/aster/tests)
          requirements:
            run:
              - ${{ compiler('fortran') }}
              - cmake
              - ${{ name }}-tests ==${{ version }}
          script:
            - run_ctest -R 'forma01a|sslp114a|mumps05a|mumps01a|umat001a|zzzz121a' --resutest=${{ env.get("OUTPUT_DIR", default="temp/seq") }}/${{ mpi }} --clean
      - if: not (is_tests_job and unix)
        then:
          # code-aster-tests is not available in the other jobs (and is only built on
          # linux): only copy the few testcases needed
          files:
            source:
              - astest/forma01a.*
              - astest/sslp114a.*
              - astest/mumps05a.*
              - astest/mumps01a.*
              - astest/umat001a.*
              - astest/zzzz121a.*
          requirements:
            run:
              - ${{ compiler('fortran') }}
              - cmake
          script:
            - if: unix
              then: run_ctest --testdir=astest -R 'forma01a|sslp114a|mumps05a|mumps01a|umat001a|zzzz121a' --resutest=${{ env.get("OUTPUT_DIR", default="temp/seq") }}/${{ mpi }} --clean
              # cmd.exe: the -R regex must be double-quoted
              # zzzz121a uses HOMARD (MACR_INFO_MAIL), which is only built on unix
              else: run_ctest --testdir=astest -R "forma01a|sslp114a|mumps05a|mumps01a|umat001a" --resutest=${{ env.get("OUTPUT_DIR", default="temp/seq") }}/${{ mpi }} --clean

about:
  license: GPL-3.0-only AND CECILL-C AND Apache-2.0 AND LGPL-3.0-only
  license_file:
    - dep-licenses/
  summary: "Code_Aster : a finite element solver"
  description: |
    Code_Aster offers a full range of multiphysical analysis and modelling methods that go well beyond the standard functions of a thermomechanical calculation code: from seismic analysis to porous media via acoustics, fatigue, stochastic dynamics, etc..
  homepage: https://www.code-aster.org
  repository: https://gitlab.com/codeaster/
  documentation: https://www.code-aster.org/V2/doc/default/en/index.php?man=commande

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - Krande
    - ldallolio
